subject: humanities
passage: For much of his career, Antonio Vivaldi taught violin at the Ospedale della Pietà, a Venetian institution that raised orphaned and abandoned girls. The best musicians among them formed an orchestra and choir whose concerts, given from behind a screen, drew visitors from across Europe. Many of the hundreds of concertos that Vivaldi wrote ______ for these performers, and the unusual difficulty of some solo parts suggests just how skilled the young women had become. Several of them, known to audiences only by a first name and an instrument, were celebrated in their own right.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The subject is "Many of the hundreds of concertos," which is plural, and the sentence needs a finite verb to be complete. The concertos did not intend anything themselves; they were intended for the performers, so the passive plural "were intended" is required.
explanation.A: Correct. "Were intended" is a finite, plural, passive verb: the concertos were meant for these performers.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Intended" on its own reads as a participle here, leaving the clause without a main verb; the concertos themselves could not have intended anything.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Was intended" is singular, but the subject "Many" is plural.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Intending" is not a finite verb, so the clause would have no main verb.
